title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over foreign intelligence concerns - Yahoo Finance Australia
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results Nvidia announced Sunday it is launching an independent investigation into its chief executive and founder, Jensen Huang, over concerns he was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort." The statement, published on the company's website, comes after US officials have expressed concern over Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, an executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. (The two are not related.) Separately, Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair in a note to staff, though he did not name the other person in the affair. The Financial Times previously reported that US intelligence provided information to US officials that the two were in a romantic relationship, according to unnamed people familiar with a memo on the intelligence, the FT reported. Nvidia is the world's leading chipmaker amid the AI boom and has a market capitalization of about $4.5 trillion. The company previously said in a statement that Jensen Huang's meetings were "not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were "debunked last year." Nvidia said a committee of independent directors and outside counsel will oversee its investigation. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the company said. But, the board "has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." "Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," a spokesperson for Nvidia told CNN. Huang, 63, said that he was "unfaithful" and hurt his wife and children in the note to Nvidia staff. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it," Huang said, adding that he supports Nvidia's investigation. "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security." President Donald Trump said Sunday that he has not spoken to Huang after Nvidia announced the investigation, but that he "probably has an excuse for it." "I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters as he left Florida. Trump also mused that he "probably has an excuse for it." Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters Sunday in Florida, declined to comment on the Nvidia situation. On Thursday, Republican chairmen of three influential House panels — the committees on Foreign Affairs, the Chinese Communist Party and Intelligence — said in a news release that they sent a letter to Huang "requesting that he appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on Huang's interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset, and NVIDIA's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage." "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the chairmen wrote. "The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress." In a note, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville & Ives Co., called the news "a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons." "The key question investors will be asking is: Will Jensen remain CEO of Nvidia?" he said. Ives also said the investigation "would increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China." This story has been updated with additional content. CNN's Logan Schiciano and Molly English contributed to this report. title: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy - CNBC
content:
Nvidia has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. U.S. intelligence agencies have expressed concerns that the woman, Alice Huang, who is affiliated with a cloud company and an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, has been passing information to Beijing, according to reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times. Huang told Nvidia staff in an email on Sunday that he had an affair with the woman and that Nvidia’s board of directors had opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” Huang wrote in the message. “I am deeply sorry.” An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption. In a statement, the Nvidia board said it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board said in a statement. Read Huang’s email to Nvidia employees and the company board of directors’ statement here. The allegations come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the U.S. as AI is seen as increasingly critical to national security. The U.S. restricts exports of Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to China, though it has approved exports of certain older, slower models. Megaspeed, which Ms. Huang is affiliated with, has been accused of helping restricted Chinese companies acquire Nvidia AI chips. Nvidia representatives previously said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. Nvidia’s Huang has pushed for broader AI chip exports to China, saying it is better for the U.S. if the world uses and builds on American technology. He has also aligned with President Donald Trump on American artificial intelligence policy and its infrastructure buildout. In his note to staff, Huang said he was “proud and grateful” to be an American. Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday asking him to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. Nvidia’s technical outlook remains bearish, with shares trading below their 50-day simple moving average (SMA) of $219.77 and 200-day SMA of $204.39. For instance, Barclays’ Thomas O’Malley has a $275 target, Bernstein’s Daniel Zhu expects $400, and Rosenblatt Securities’ Kevin Cassidy sees $390. Meanwhile, banking giant Morgan Stanley has reaffirmed Nvidia as its top semiconductor pick, maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating and a $288 price target. Nvidia’s correction reflects concerns about AI infrastructure spending and geopolitical risks. Notably, on Friday, NVDA shares had lost approximately $450 billion in market value following its November 5 decline, with the sell-off also affecting semiconductor peers such as Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD). Investors are concerned that tougher AI regulations and delays in data center construction could slow spending by Nvidia’s largest customers. Delays involving infrastructure, power connections, and regulatory approvals could also affect orders and revenue. Meanwhile, despite its lower forward earnings multiple, Nvidia remains vulnerable to concerns that AI spending could peak sooner than expected. China presents another risk after approximately 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips were held in Hong Kong pending approval for shipment to mainland China. Beijing has yet to authorize large-scale imports and is encouraging domestic companies to prioritize local alternatives. title: Dan Ives Says NVDA's Recent Underperformance Is A Bump Than Anything Else — 'There's One Chip In The World Fueling The AI Revolution' - Stocktwits
content: Tech strategist Dan Ives on Monday downplayed concerns around Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) recent underperformance, calling it just a speed bump rather than anything else. During an interview with CNBC, Ives added that the underperformance of Nvidia and other hyperscalers is due more to the market flocking to memory stocks, calling it the “shiny new toy” effect. “You’ve seen so many of these names, when the ones that are actually at the center, whether it’s the hyperscalers or Nvidia… those are actually the ones, to some extent, almost in the penalty box,” he said. Nvidia shares were down more than 1% in Monday’s pre-market trade. Ives highlighted a disconnect between the AI trade and the companies fueling the AI revolution. “The reality is, there’s one chip in the world fueling the AI revolution, that’s by the godfather of AI the revolution, Jensen of Nvidia,” he said. Nvidia’s forward price-to-earnings ratio is currently hovering around 21.2, according to data from Koyfin, recovering slightly after falling to 19.6 last week, levels that were seen in January 2019. “When you look at memory, where is memory with Nvidia? Where's memory without hyperscalers? This all plays into what's going to be a crucial earnings season in Q2 for monetization,” he said. Ives added that he continues to see chip demand far outstripping supply, estimating the demand-to-supply ratio at 15-to-1. Ives said that the U.S. listing of SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY) is just the start, after the South Korean DRAM manufacturer raised $26.5 billion last week and debuted on Nasdaq at $170 per American Depositary Receipt (ADR), compared with an issue price of $149. “The reality is, for the first time in 30 years, the U.S. is ahead of China when it comes to tech. I think what you saw with SK, you’re going to see more and more companies tap the U.S. market,” he added. Ives also noted that the U.S. offers these companies not just liquidity but is also at the center of the AI trade. The tech strategist described Apple Inc.’s (AAPL) lawsuit against OpenAI as the iPhone maker defending its turf, adding that others in Silicon Valley will be watching what Apple does with OpenAI. “For Apple, it’s a shot across the bow. They’re basically saying, no más. This needs to stop. I think it’s important to what they’re doing, because they’re defending their turf, as well as with Google and Gemini, they finally have an AI strategy,” he said. Apple sued OpenAI in federal court in California last Friday, alleging a widespread effort to steal its trade secrets. The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI directed current and former Apple employees to provide confidential documents, product blueprints, and physical components. Apple claims the effort was orchestrated by OpenAI's leadership to accelerate the development of its own competing AI devices. NVDA stock is up 13% year-to-date and 29% over the past 12 months. Late Sunday, HIMS published an Instagram carousel explaining what peptides are, why they have attracted biohackers and how they could become part of mainstream healthcare. The campaign comes as investors search for Hims’ next major growth engine beyond compounded GLP-1 drugs, and as regulators prepare to decide whether seven popular peptides should receive a clearer pathway into the U.S. compounding market. Hims said more than 170 peptides are in active clinical development, presenting the category as established science rather than a passing wellness trend. “Peptides aren’t new—they’ve been researched for decades,” the post said. “What’s changed? Research is growing, and peptides are becoming part of mainstream health conversations.” The final slide also acknowledged one of the market’s biggest challenges: inconsistent sourcing and formulation. “Not all peptides are created equal,” Hims said. “The science is real. Quality is what makes the difference.” The campaign comes ahead of the FDA’s July 23-24 Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meeting, where members will consider adding BPC-157, Emideltide, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax and TB-500 to the Section 503A Bulks List. FDA staff have recommended against all seven, citing limited human evidence, unclear formulations and unresolved risks including immune reactions and contamination. Former committee member Dr. Anita Gupta said earlier reviews raised “some red flags” over immunogenicity and pointed to reports of “heavy metals,” “microbial contamination” and mislabeling. The Partnership for Safe Medicines also urged rejection, saying the evidence is dominated by animal studies, laboratory research and weak overseas trials. It noted that BPC-157 has fewer than 36 human participants across three studies, KPV has no live-human trials and TB-500 has only one human tolerance study. The group also warned that compounding could falsely signal FDA approval and cited 127 peptide shipments entering U.S. ports in the first quarter, with about 39% coming from manufacturers outside FDA oversight. title: NVIDIA Or Micron: Where Each Leads In The AI Buildout - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Investors buy both NVIDIA (NVDA) and Micron Technology (MU) to capture the spending on AI data centers: NVIDIA sells the computing systems, and Micron sells DRAM and NAND memory. Micron trades at 9.2 times earnings compared with 23.4 for NVIDIA, making it look like the cheaper way in. Yet NVIDIA said in August that soaring memory prices had prompted a reset of its gross margin expectations. So will memory prices keep rising, and can NVIDIA keep growing while it pays them? They are, although Micron expects the increases to slow. During its August 26, 2026 call, NVIDIA said memory price increases had exceeded its expectations and were headed even higher. For NVIDIA, that serves as a cost warning, but for Micron, those same prices are what it sells at. Micron provided a pricing outlook on its September 30 call. Management guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $60 billion to $63 billion, compared with $54.2 billion in fiscal Q4 2026. That forecast assumes only single-digit growth in the bits of DRAM and NAND that Micron ships, leaving price and product mix to supply the rest of the rise. Management also said price increases would continue at a more moderate pace. Micron’s 86.0% guide for its gross margin sits just below the 86.8% it reported for fiscal Q4. So far it can, although its margin is slipping. NVIDIA guided fiscal Q3 2027 revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, compared with $96.2 billion in fiscal Q2. Management expects fiscal 2028 revenue to grow about 70% and said supply, including of its new Vera Rubin systems, would remain the bottleneck through at least the end of that year. The memory bill shows up in the margin instead. NVIDIA reported a 75.0% gross margin for fiscal Q2 and guided 74% for fiscal Q3, plus or minus half a point. Management expects it to bottom at 71% to 72% in fiscal Q4, then settle at 72% to 73% in fiscal 2028 as NVIDIA’s own price increases take effect. NVIDIA’s margins have also been far steadier than those of Micron. NVIDIA’s operating margin averaged 61.7% over the last three twelve-month periods, compared with 35.3% for Micron. Over those periods, NVIDIA’s twelve-month operating margin stayed between 58.1% and 65.2%, while Micron’s twelve-month operating margin climbed from 5.2% to 74.6% in two years. Over the latest twelve months, Micron comes out ahead on growth and margin. Micron’s revenue grew 256.3%, against 83.4% for NVIDIA. Its operating margin was 74.6%, compared with 65.2% for NVIDIA. Each company has debt under 1% of its market value. You cannot see from Micron’s low multiple how new its profits are. Micron’s quarterly operating margin was 45.0% in fiscal Q1 2026 and 80.7% by fiscal Q4. If memory prices fall, Micron stands to lose that margin, and its multiple would look less cheap on lower earnings. If NVIDIA’s growth stalls instead, you lose the growth its higher multiple pays for, as set out in a sales forecast that runs a full year ahead. Each stock has its own way to disappoint. A portfolio ready for a crash and a rally doesn’t need you to pick. Micron leads on its multiple, growth and margin over the latest twelve months, and memory prices are still rising. NVIDIA leads on how steady its margins have been, and its growth outlook holds even as memory costs pull its gross margin down. The memory prices behind Micron’s margin may rise more slowly from here, because Micron’s own management expects the increases to moderate. Micron’s gross margin for fiscal Q1 2027 is the number to watch when it reports in December 2026. If you own an S&P 500 or Nasdaq fund, you already own NVIDIA, alongside the same few giants that lead those funds. title: Cathie Wood-Led Ark Loads Up On GOOG, AMD, NVDA And Biotech Stocks — But Sells CRWV, AVGO, LLY - Stocktwits

The latest round of trades touched multiple ARK ETFs, spanning artificial intelligence, semiconductors, biotechnology, defense and space-related companies. The activity also included changes to some of the firm's cryptocurrency and healthcare holdings. Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) featured among ARK's notable purchases, with the investment firm adding shares through ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). The buying also extended to semiconductor heavyweights Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), both of which saw additions through ARKW. ARK also continued buying into the defense and aerospace space. Kratos Defense & Security Solutions Inc. (KTOS) was purchased across three ETFs, namely, ARKK, ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) and ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX). Ark added to positions in AeroVironment Inc. (AVAV), Joby Aviation Inc. (JOBY), Intuitive Machines Inc. (LUNR) and Rocket Lab Corp. (RKLB) through ARKX. Healthcare and biotechnology names featured prominently in the buying activity as well. ARK added to Natera Inc. (NTRA) through both ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG) and ARKK, alongside purchases of Tempus AI Inc. (TEM), Twist Bioscience Corp. (TWST), 10x Genomics Inc. (TXG), Scribe Therapeutics Inc. (SCTX) and Iambic Therapeutics Inc. (IAM). ARKW also picked up shares of Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS), while ARKK added to its Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN) position. On the selling side, CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) and Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) were among the prominent technology names trimmed through ARKK. The ETF also reduced its position in Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY), alongside sales of Teradyne Inc. (TER) and Bullish (BLSH). Bullish was sold across three funds, namely, ARK Blockchain & Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF), ARKK and ARKW, making it one of the more widespread reductions in Friday's trading activity. ARK's other sales included BYD Co. Ltd. (BYDDY) through ARKQ, while ARKG reduced its holdings in CareDx Inc. (CDNA) and Personalis Inc. (PSNL). ARKX also trimmed Teradyne. Mike McGlone, Senior Commodity Strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, doubled down on his call for Bitcoin (BTC) to fall to $10,000, saying that he believes the next stock bear market has already started. McGlone said he had first made the call in the first quarter of 2025, when Bitcoin traded above $100,000, and said that the outlook had remained unchanged. "The call from 1Q25 with Bitcoin above $100,000 was for it to lose a zero, on the back of a 20% drawdown in the S&P 500 (SPX) that stays down awhile, remains my base case," he wrote on X on Friday. A Bitcoin price that "loses a zero" would fall about 90%, to roughly $10,000. McGlone said that level carried the weight for the asset, noting that "10,000 Bitcoin is a key pivot." He also drew a link between crypto and stocks, saying that Bitcoin peaked on October 6 last year, while the Nasdaq peaked exactly a year later, on October 6, 2026. “May the market gods be with us all when we have the next stock bear market. I think it has started," he said. Bitcoin's price was trading at $75,830, up 0.2% during the past 24 hours, while the S&P 500 closed at 7,376 points on Friday, about 6% below its 52-week high of 7,844. That was well short of the 20% drop McGlone said would push Bitcoin toward $10,000. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day. McGlone's post came in response to crypto trader and well-known investor Scott Melker, famously known as the "Wolf of All Streets." He said that the stock sell-off had not hit Bitcoin as hard as bears had expected. "Nasdaq entered correction territory today, more than 10% below its recent high," Melker said on X. Melker said the market had already covered half the drop that was meant to drag Bitcoin down. "The Nasdaq is down 10%, and we're still 17 or $18,000 above Bitcoin's low," he said. "The case that the Nasdaq or the market dropping 20% would send Bitcoin to $10,000, to me, or something way lower right now does not make any sense because we're halfway there." VanEck Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jan van Eck said that the next U.S. financial crisis would begin in Washington rather than in the banking system, and said investors should hold "real assets" like gold and Bitcoin (BTC) as protection. In an interview with Anthony Pompliano on Thursday, van Eck said, "For the entirety of U.S. history," financial crises have started with banks. This time, however, he expected the trouble to come from government debt. "This is going to be started in D.C. and no one can bail us out. And I think the rest of the world sees this," he said. That outlook shaped his view on portfolios. When asked how investors could protect themselves from U.S. government spending, van Eck pointed to hard assets. "You have to have real assets, gold and Bitcoin in your portfolio. You don't know if it'll pay off," he said. He was clear about his position on Bitcoin over the longer run, and said, "I'm a long-term bull, so I definitely think it would be higher in 10 years. Van Eck saw no easy way out for Washington, and said, "We're going to inflate our way out of our debt." "There's no easy answer, and it's not going to be pretty." He also dismissed the idea that artificial intelligence (AI) would ease the pressure by pushing prices down. "All technology is deflationary," he said. "There was great technology in the 70s, but we had runaway inflation." Bitcoin's price was down by 0.2% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day. Rather than adding more crypto products, VanEck is now pushing active management. He said it made sense because most financial advisers struggled to choose between tokens like Avalanche (AVAX) and Ethereum (ETH). "Most advisors can't pick Avalanche versus Ethereum or these kinds of things," he said. According to the VanEck CEO, layer-1 blockchains, the base networks that other crypto applications run on, along with the trading platforms, would hold up. "The foundational ones will survive, I think, and then the exchanges, I think, will survive," he said. For investors who want exposure beyond those two groups, van Eck's advice was to leave token picking to a fund. "Otherwise, go with an index or go with an active managed fund," he said. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Bitcoin (BTC) slipped to the brink of its 50-week moving average on Friday, threatening a run of weekly closes above the key trend line. The apex cryptocurrency traded at around $76,000, leaving it 0.6% above its 50-week simple moving average (SMA) of $75,580. The 50-week SMA is the average closing price of Bitcoin over the past 50 weeks, or around a year, and is typically viewed by traders as an indicator of the long-term trend. The slide began on Thursday when Bitcoin posted its biggest single-day loss since June, falling 5.5% from about $80,100 to $75,700. The selloff continued on Thursday, with the price hitting a low of $74,720. That briefly put it about 1.1% below average. Bitcoin recovered by the end of the session and closed back above the line at $75,800. Bitcoin has only just moved back above the average. It finished the week of September 20 at $81,150, Cointelegraph reported, citing TradingView data. At the time, the 50-week moving average was around $78,780. It was Bitcoin's first weekly close above the line since November 9, 2025. Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, has been closely following the level. In a research note in August, he had said the 50-week average had served as a ceiling in past bear markets. In four out of the five bear markets that have ended, the first break above the bottom was the bottom. Galaxy also warned that the signal was not foolproof. Of 13 weekly crosses back above the average in past bear markets, two were followed by a lower low, both during the 2021-2022 downturn. Bitcoin closed above the line for seven weeks in a row as of the close of the week ended Nov. 1. That close was $78,220, or 3.3% above the average, according to Galaxy. Since then, the cushion has shrunk to well below 1%. At the time of writing, Bitcoin’s price was trading at $75,990, flat over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day. Bitcoin was down about 5.5% from its 10-week simple moving average of $80,522, according to data from Koyfin. The 10-week line moved above the 50-week line in October but was starting to flatten. The 50-week average was still heading lower, and it was down from over $100,000 at the start of the year, according to Koyfin. The next test comes at the weekly close on Nov. 8, and a finish above the 50-week line would make it eight weeks straight. A break below it would be the first one since the September reclaim and could revive fears of a false breakout. content: Chip stocks had their worst day since 2020. Here is what it did to one retiree's 1,000 Nvidia shares, and the case for holding or trimming. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) shareholders just lived through the roughest week for chip stocks in more than five years. On Thursday, the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 12.25%, its biggest one-day drop since March 2020, as investors weighed what the new Congress could mean for data center construction. Nvidia fell 9.26% that day to $181.60. On Friday it bounced 2.78% to close at $186.64. Even after the bounce, Nvidia ended the week 8.8% lower and sits 22% below its record close of $239.24 on Oct. 6. Take a 64-year-old retiree who bought 1,000 shares on June 10, 2024, the day Nvidia’s 10-for-1 split took effect, at $121.79 a share. That was a $121,790 investment. At the October record the shares were worth $239,240. On Friday they were worth $186,640. They also hold $600,000 in other retirement savings and collect $2,500 a month from Social Security, so Nvidia is now 23.7% of a $786,640 portfolio. The question this weekend is whether Thursday was a warning to sell. The sell-off hit almost every chip name at once. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell 12.15%, its worst day since March 2020, and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF fell 11.21%. Micron fell 17.46% and Lam Research 16.36%. Nvidia’s 9.26% drop was one of the smaller ones. That gap matters. The stocks that fell hardest sell equipment and memory, which depend on what chipmakers and data center owners plan to spend next year. Nvidia sells into demand that exists today. Investors were pricing in a slowdown in future spending more than a drop in current orders. Friday brought some relief. Chip stocks rebounded across the board, and Nvidia traded as high as $194.90 during the day before settling at $186.64. Measured from the purchase, the investment is still well ahead. The 1,000 shares cost $121,790 and are worth $186,640, a gain of $64,850, or 53.2%, in under two and a half years. Measured from the peak, the shares have given back $52,600 in a month. Thursday alone took $18,530, and Friday returned $5,040 of it. Nvidia also pays more than it used to. It raised its quarterly dividend to 25 cents a share this year, from 1 cent. On 1,000 shares that is $1,000 a year, a yield of 0.54% at Friday’s price. The dividend is small next to the price swings, but it is a sign the company is generating more cash than it needs. The business is still growing at a pace few large companies have ever matched. Nvidia’s revenue over the past four reported quarters reached $302.97 billion, and its latest quarter’s revenue was up 105.9% from a year earlier. The stock is also cheaper than it looks after a run like this. At $186.64, Nvidia trades at about 23.6 times its earnings over the past year. Of the 62 analysts tracked, 59 rate it a buy or strong buy, and their average price target is $327.14, about 75% above Friday’s close. The next real test is close. Nvidia reports its quarterly results later this month, and that report will show whether customers are still ordering at the pace they were. The risk for this retiree is concentration. Nvidia is 23.7% of everything they own, and at the October peak it was 28.5%. A stock that can fall 9% in a day can fall 30% over a few months. A 30% drop from here would cost about $55,992, almost two years of the $30,000 a year Social Security pays them. Well-known skeptics are still betting against the sector. Michael Burry disclosed this week that he took profits on a quarter of his bet against the VanEck Semiconductor ETF after Thursday’s plunge, and said the rest of the position remains very large. Selling part of the position is a reasonable option. If the retiree sells 300 of the 1,000 shares at Friday’s price: If the shares sit in a traditional IRA, the sale itself creates no tax bill today. Trimming keeps most of the upside if the analysts are right and the next report is strong. It also moves some of a paper gain into cash before the report, when the stock is likely to swing again. No one knows whether Thursday was the start of a longer slide or a sharp one-day scare. The analyst targets were mostly set before this week. And the $2,918 tax figure assumes the retiree’s income keeps them in the 15% long-term capital gains bracket; a larger sale could push part of the gain higher. A 64-year-old who turned $121,790 into $186,640 with Nvidia is still well ahead, even after losing $18,530 on the chip sector’s worst day since 2020. The bigger question is whether 23.7% of a retirement should ride on one stock heading into its next earnings report. title: NVDA Stock Rebounds 4% but $180 Support Remains Critical After Midterm Selloff for Nvidia - FXLeaders
content: Nvidia shares extended their decline from record highs above $243, falling towards $181 before recovering 4% on Friday, as Democratic midterm victories, rising infrastructure costs, electricity constraints and growing opposition to data-centre expansion intensified concerns about the semiconductor industry’s growth prospects. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) shares dropped below $200 on Thursday, falling towards $181 and extending their retreat from record highs above $243. The stock attempted a recovery on Friday, gaining approximately 4%, but buyers failed to push it back above the psychological $200 level, leaving shares close to the important $180 support zone. The latest weakness reflects growing concerns about the enormous infrastructure commitments underpinning semiconductor valuations. Investors are increasingly questioning whether major technology companies can maintain their current investment pace as financing costs rise, electricity availability becomes more challenging and political resistance to new data-centre developments gains momentum. The Democratic victories in the US midterm elections have introduced another challenge for Nvidia and the broader semiconductor industry. Gina Hinojosa’s victory in Texas, alongside political changes in Ohio and Georgia involving Amy Acton and Keisha Lance Bottoms, has strengthened opposition to unchecked data-centre expansion. Proposals for restrictions and freezes on new developments highlight growing concerns about electricity consumption, water requirements and rising utility bills. Reports that 40 of 41 direct votes concerning data-centre projects failed further illustrate the changing public sentiment. For Nvidia, the implications could extend beyond political headlines. Delays in construction, additional regulatory requirements and higher infrastructure expenses could affect the spending plans of major cloud providers, which remain among the company’s most important customers. Electricity availability is becoming a significant bottleneck for the infrastructure industry. Technology companies may increasingly need to finance additional power generation and grid improvements rather than relying entirely on existing electricity networks. Financing conditions are also creating pressure. CoreWeave has faced growing scrutiny as yields on some of its debt maturing in 2032 approached 15%, highlighting the risks associated with heavily leveraged infrastructure expansion. Amazon has reportedly experienced delays involving Nvidia-equipped server racks waiting in warehouses because certain data centres lack sufficient electricity to operate them. These developments raise questions about construction schedules, capital efficiency and whether the enormous investments being made will generate sufficient returns. NVIDIA shares lost momentum early in September after failing to break decisively above the $236 resistance zone, with the rejection sending the stock back below $210 but we have seen a decent rebound recently. Shares have climbed above $233 today as investors responded positively to expanding infrastructure partnerships and CEO projections, but buyers are not able to sustain the rally above $243 and we saw dive to $180 today where NVDA is testing the last support at the 100 weekly SMA in green. The trend will depend on whether the 100 SMA holds as support. Despite the share-price weakness, Nvidia continues strengthening its position across the semiconductor supply chain. CEO Jensen Huang reportedly consulted with Marvell Technology and Lumentum executives ahead of Marvell’s approximately $115 billion enterprise-value acquisition of Lumentum. Nvidia previously invested $2 billion in each company, increasing its exposure to optical networking and connectivity technologies required for expanding data-centre infrastructure. However, the transaction also highlights the enormous capital requirements associated with building the next generation of computing infrastructure. Demand for computing capacity remains substantial. Anthropic reportedly plans to increase its computing capacity beyond 3.5 gigawatts by the end of 2026, potentially reaching approximately 7 gigawatts in 2027. Samsung Electronics is also preparing to manufacture base dies for high-bandwidth memory chips intended for Nvidia and AMD, with mass production targeted for 2030. However, Nvidia is facing increasing competition from custom processors. Google and Oracle plan to make Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure from 2027, providing customers with another alternative to Nvidia-powered systems. Although Nvidia retains considerable advantages through its software ecosystem, performance and established customer relationships, expanding competition could eventually put pressure on pricing and market share. The technical picture has deteriorated significantly following the decline below $200. Friday’s 4% rebound provides some relief, but buyers have yet to reclaim this important psychological level. The immediate focus remains on $180 support. A sustained break below this area could expose further downside towards $150, while a recovery above $200 would be needed to improve the short-term outlook. Nvidia remains a major semiconductor player with substantial exposure to long-term computing demand. Nevertheless, investors are increasingly questioning whether infrastructure spending can continue at its previous pace. For now, sellers retain control of the technical picture, while political opposition, electricity shortages, financing risks and growing competition could keep Nvidia shares under pressure.

title: What’s Going To Happen With NVIDIA Stock Soon? - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. NVIDIA (NVDA) stock fell 9.3% on November 5, 2026, marking its largest one-day drop in a year. Shareholders also face a strain management has already acknowledged. During its August 26, 2026 call, management said NVIDIA’s gross margin would get worse before it got better. Below are the reports and events most likely to move NVIDIA stock over the next six months. NVIDIA is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2027 results on November 17, 2026. This will be the company’s first report since that August call. Management guided revenue to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, compared with $96.2 billion in fiscal Q2 2027. The guide counts no data center sales to China. Management left those sales out of its outlook because of geopolitical uncertainty. In fiscal Q2 2027, NVIDIA’s shipments of Hopper 200 products to customers in China came to less than 1% of its data center revenue. Revenue against that guide is the figure to watch in November 2026. NVIDIA expects its gross margin to dip because of memory. Management said in August 2026 that memory prices had risen more than it expected and were still heading higher. Management guided gross margin to a low of 71% to 72% in fiscal Q4 2027, down from 75% in fiscal Q2 2027. For fiscal Q3 2027, it guided gross margin to 74%, plus or minus 50 basis points. The drop matters at NVIDIA’s size. Each point of gross margin on its $303 billion of revenue over the past twelve months is worth about $3 billion a year. Management expects the margin to edge back up in fiscal 2028, as price increases NVIDIA has already set take effect. The gross margin NVIDIA reports for fiscal Q4 2027 is the figure to watch, with results expected in February 2027. NVIDIA began production shipments of Vera Rubin, the platform that follows Blackwell, in August 2026. Purchase orders are already in from every major hyperscaler. Management expected Vera Rubin to make up about 20% of data center revenue in fiscal Q3 2027. Data center revenue as a whole was $89 billion in fiscal Q2 2027. NVIDIA also expects growth in sales to hyperscalers, the largest cloud companies, to pick up again in fiscal Q4 2027 as Vera Rubin supply grows. For now, management expects growth to come mainly from its NeoCloud, industrial and enterprise customers. The limit is supply rather than orders. Management expects supply to remain a bottleneck at least through the end of fiscal 2028. Growth in NVIDIA’s sales to hyperscalers is the measure to watch when it reports in February 2027. Owning the stock through these reports means being ready for a fall like the one it has just taken. The stock dropped 24.1% from its October 6, 2026 close to November 5, marking the largest drop of the past year. That fall took 22 trading sessions and came before either report. Rattled by November 5? It has happened 21 times before. Here’s what came next. If a second fall of that size would push you to sell, the holding is larger than you can carry through the November 2026 and February 2027 reports.
